items.title: Manny Gabriel Interview, 1965-07-27
items.q: That's right, he was something. He'd done it with us, you know.

ctx.x: Now he plays the trombone at this hand and the trumpet at this hand. Yeah. He puts the strap around and plays the trombone and the trumpet. That's really good.

I know one thing, if this clarinet was broke, all these keys here, one or two of these keys can't come down or anything, and they just plug them up there and he'd play that clarinet just like nothing ain't happen. That's right, he was something. He'd done it with us, you know. That's all right, don't play two, three, four, five keys. Play it right on. Yeah, he was a great clarinet player. He played a whole lot of clarinet, he played a whole lot of piano, and he had the chords and trumpet. I know he could play it…

Yeah, well, yeah. Although he's about retired, he doesn't do much. He's seventy-five years old now. Yeah, he ought to be around there. He was a nice-looking man when he was here. Yeah, he was a nice-looking man when he was here. Yeah, he still looks good. He was very sick a year ago, had an operation, but he pulled out of it all right and got over looks better than he did a few years ago.
